body:
### Description

The following arrays give an apparently incorrect overflowed result with matmul. 

```py
>>> import cupy as cp
>>> x = cp.asarray([51307], dtype=cp.uint16)
>>> y = cp.asarray([[[327]]], dtype=cp.uint16)
>>> x
array([51307], dtype=uint16)
>>> y
array([[[327]]], dtype=uint16)
>>> x @ y # This is giving a different answer
array([[172]], dtype=uint16)
>>> x*y
array([[[173]]], dtype=uint16)
>>> x @ y[0]
array([173], dtype=uint16)
>>> x * y[0]
array([[173]], dtype=uint16)
```

The error only occurs when the second array has 3 dimensions. Presumably cupy uses different code paths for stacked vs. non-stacked linear algebra functions. Note that `51307*327 % 2**16` is indeed `173`.

I'm unclear whether this behavior is actually a bug or if this is something that is to be expected from overflowing integers. 

I identified this with the array API test suite, but it is unrelated to the array API module. The array API doesn't specify overflow behavior, but it would be simpler in the test suite if it could just ignore overflowing.

```py
# Write the code here
```
